problem: Neural networks degrade substantially when label error rates exceed a threshold, limiting their ability to learn from noisy datasets common in real-world labeling scenarios.
approach: Proposes Rockafellian Relaxation Method (RRM), a loss reweighting wrapper that modifies any methodology's supervised training loss to better accommodate noisy labeled data.
contribution: RRM improves accuracy across computer vision and NLP classification tasks regardless of dataset size, noise type, data domain, and adversarial perturbation.

problem: Robotic control tasks require policies to act on orientations, but SO(3) lacks a global smooth minimal parameterization, making it unclear which rotation representation works best for reinforcement learning.
approach: Systematically evaluates SO(3) action representations (Euler angles, quaternions, rotation matrices, Lie algebra) across three RL algorithms (PPO, SAC, TD3) under different reward settings.
contribution: Shows that tangent vectors in the local frame yield the most reliable results, providing implementation-ready guidelines for selecting rotation actions in robotic control.

problem: Existing generative models struggle to handle genuine freehand sketches with their inherent abstraction and distortions, lacking effective algorithms that balance photorealism with sketch adherence.
approach: Proposes a modulation-based approach that prioritizes semantic interpretation over strict pixel-aligned adherence, with a novel loss enabling training without ground-truth pixel-aligned images.
contribution: Outperforms existing methods in semantic alignment with freehand sketch inputs and generates images with superior realism and quality.

problem: Skill-based meta-RL methods are highly susceptible to noisy offline demonstrations, leading to unstable skill learning and degraded performance in long-horizon environments.
approach: Proposes Self-Improving Skill Learning (SISL) with decoupled high-level and skill improvement policies, using maximum return relabeling to prioritize task-relevant trajectories.
contribution: Achieves robust and stable adaptation under noisy and suboptimal data, consistently outperforming other skill-based meta-RL methods on diverse long-horizon tasks.

problem: Knowledge graph-augmented LLMs suffer from search space truncation bias and entity error amplification when handling multi-hop reasoning and complex logical queries.
approach: Proposes Plan-Answer-Refine-on-Graph (PARoG), which decomposes SPARQL queries into structured step-by-step plans and adopts a plan-answer-refine paradigm to integrate evidence from KGs.
contribution: Substantially reduces hallucinations and improves logical consistency on multiple KG reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Deep learning models suffer from loss of plasticity in non-stationary environments, but prior literature lacks mechanistic explanation for why gradient descent fails to recover from these states.
approach: Presents a first-principles investigation using dynamical systems theory, formally defining loss of plasticity as entrapment within invariant sub-manifolds caused by frozen units and cloned-unit manifolds.
contribution: Uncovers that mechanisms promoting generalization in static settings actively steer networks into loss-of-plasticity manifolds, and shows architectural interventions can destabilize these manifolds.

problem: Diffusion language models are slower than autoregressive models due to bidirectional attention costs and many refinement steps needed for high-quality outputs.
approach: Introduces Prophet, a training-free fast decoding paradigm that uses confidence gap between top-2 predictions to decide early stopping, enabling early commit decoding.
contribution: Reduces decoding steps by up to 3.4x while preserving generation quality on GSM8K and MMLU, with up to 99% of instances decoded correctly using half refinement steps.

problem: Tool retrieval for LLMs is hindered by incomplete and heterogeneous tool documentation, limiting effective tool use despite LLMs' strong capabilities.
approach: Introduces Tool-DE benchmark and framework that enriches tool documentation with structured fields via LLM-driven document expansion, developing Tool-Embed (dense retriever) and Tool-Rank (reranker).
contribution: Document expansion substantially improves retrieval performance, achieving state-of-the-art on both ToolRet and Tool-DE benchmarks with 50k and 200k instances respectively.

problem: Existing routing systems for AI task computation require retraining whenever new strategies appear and struggle with generalization using single input representations.
approach: Proposes CONCUR, a modular continual routing framework with separate predictor models per strategy and multiple representations to capture task complexity.
contribution: Outperforms single-strategy and existing routing methods on in-distribution and out-of-distribution tasks with higher accuracy and lower inference cost while reducing training cost.

problem: Existing open-source multimodal models lack rich feature sets for visual reasoning like image manipulation and code-based computation found in proprietary models.
approach: Introduces Thyme, enabling multimodal LLMs to autonomously generate and execute diverse image processing operations via executable code, with SFT on 500K samples and RL via GRPO-ATS.
contribution: Enables models to perform rich on-the-fly image manipulations and mathematical computations while maintaining high autonomy in deciding when and how to apply operations.

problem: Existing red-teaming benchmarks fail when adapted via direct translation, missing socio-technical vulnerabilities rooted in local culture and law.
approach: Proposes CAGE framework that systematically adapts adversarial intent of red-teaming prompts to new cultural contexts via Semantic Mold, disentangling adversarial structure from cultural content.
contribution: Demonstrates framework via KoRSET Korean benchmark, proving more effective at revealing vulnerabilities than direct translation baselines.

problem: Density ratio estimation methods are highly sensitive to hyperparameter selection, with suboptimal choices leading to poor convergence and empirical performance.
approach: Proposes a novel model aggregation algorithm that trains multiple models with different hyperparameters and aggregates them, achieving minimax-optimal convergence without prior smoothness knowledge.
contribution: Achieves minimax-optimal error convergence, surpassing cross-validation and model averaging baselines on standard benchmarks and large-scale domain adaptation tasks.

problem: While image-text alignment is well-studied, the temporal nature of video data remains largely unexplored in cross-modal representation alignment.
approach: Conducts first comprehensive study of video-text representation alignment using state-of-the-art video and language encoders, proposing parametric test-time scaling laws.
contribution: Shows alignment depends on richness of visual and text data provided at test time, and strong alignment correlates with general-purpose video representation and temporal reasoning.

problem: LLMs in multi-agent systems suffer from rapport bias, over-relying on previous interactions and peer input while resisting misinformation during collaboration.
approach: Introduces KAIROS benchmark simulating quiz contests with varying peer reliability, evaluating prompting, fine-tuning, and GRPO across multiple models.
contribution: Shows larger models are more resilient to social influence via prompting, while smaller models benefit from GRPO-based mitigation, improving both robustness and performance.

problem: Classical optimal transport with full-mass or fixed-mass preservation is too restrictive for applications requiring adaptive-mass transport between distributions.
approach: Proposes Elastic Optimal Transport (ELOT) enabling adaptive-mass preservation, with applications to unsupervised and partial domain adaptation.
contribution: ELOT significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods on domain adaptation benchmarks while respecting data noise and outliers.

problem: LLMs excel at generating text but their internal reasoning remains opaque and lack systematic mechanisms for reasoning or model control.
approach: Proposes ActivationReasoning (AR), embedding explicit logical reasoning into LLM latent space via SAEs, detecting activating concepts and mapping to logical propositions for inference.
contribution: Scales robustly with reasoning complexity, generalizes to abstract tasks, transfers across models, and improves transparency and reliable control.

problem: Existing optimization-based jailbreak methods rely heavily on sparse success signals or manually-crafted scoring templates introducing human bias.
approach: Introduces AMIS, a meta-optimization framework jointly evolving jailbreak prompts and scoring templates through bi-level structure with inner-loop prompt refinement and outer-loop template optimization.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance with 88.0% ASR on Claude-3.5-Haiku and 100.0% ASR on Claude-4-Sonnet, substantially outperforming baselines.

problem: Vision Transformers lack a mechanistic account of their computational phenomenology despite architectural hints at dynamical structure.
approach: Introduces Block-Recurrent Hypothesis (BRH) showing trained ViTs admit block-recurrent depth structure rewritable with fewer distinct blocks applied recurrently, operationalized via Raptor.
contribution: Recovers 94% of DINOv2 ImageNet-1k accuracy using only 2 blocks, providing dynamical interpretability framework for Vision Transformers.

problem: Squared tensor networks and circuits suffer from computational complexity in marginalization due to squaring operation, hindering applicability in machine learning.
approach: Parameterizes squared circuits via unitary matrices enabling efficient marginalization in factorizations beyond standard tensor networks.
contribution: Unlocks efficient marginalization in diverse circuit structures without expressiveness loss while enabling more efficient learning.

problem: Existing benchmarks fail to assess multi-image spatial reasoning that real-world multimodal LLM deployments demand, only probing single-image relations.
approach: Introduces MMSI-Bench, a VQA benchmark with 1,000 carefully crafted multiple-choice questions from 120,000 images, featuring automated error analysis diagnosing four failure modes.
contribution: Reveals wide gap between open-source (≈30%) and proprietary models (40% for GPT-5), identifies dominant failure modes including grounding and spatial-logic errors.

problem: Differentially private continual release of distinct items requires polynomial additive error even in turnstile streams with insertions and deletions.
approach: Shows additive error lower bounds can be circumvented by allowing multiplicative error, achieving polylog(T) multiplicative and additive error.
contribution: Demonstrates trade-off between multiplicative and additive error in private continual estimation, opening new directions for privacy-utility balance.

problem: Obtaining high-quality evaluation metrics for AI models is costly, requiring trade-offs between expensive high-quality measurements and cheaper lower-quality proxies.
approach: Introduces Multiple-Prediction-Powered Inference (MultiPPI), optimally allocating resources across diverse data sources with minimax-optimal guarantees.
contribution: Consistently achieves lower estimation error than baselines on LLM evaluation tasks through budget-adaptive allocation learning complex cost and correlation structures.

problem: Estimating latent triggering kernels for Hawkes processes in RKHS framework typically requires costly optimization to obtain dual coefficients.
approach: Establishes a novel representer theorem showing dual coefficients are analytically fixed to unity via penalized least squares, eliminating optimization overhead.
contribution: Achieves competitive predictive accuracy while substantially improving computational efficiency over state-of-the-art kernel-based estimators on large-scale data.

problem: LLM output contains repetitive lexical patterns (slop) that degrade writing quality and make AI-generated text immediately recognizable.
approach: Proposes Antislop framework combining Antislop Sampler for inference-time suppression, automated slop profiling pipeline, and Final Token Preference Optimization for fine-tuning.
contribution: Some patterns appear 1,000x more frequently in LLM output than human text; achieves 90% slop reduction while maintaining quality on GSM8K, MMLU, and creative writing.

problem: Tool-use RL relies exclusively on sparse outcome rewards and lacks consideration of task structure, inflating policy-gradient variance and resulting in inefficient training.
approach: Proposes Reshaped Token-level policy gradients (ResT) that reshape policy gradients through entropy-informed token reweighting, progressively upweighting reasoning tokens.
contribution: Outperforms baselines on BFCL and API-Bank by up to 8.76%, and fine-tuned 4B model surpasses GPT-4o by 4.11% on single-turn tasks.

problem: Existing trajectory representation methods assume smooth motion and struggle with event-driven annotation, abrupt changes, GPS errors, and domain shifts.
approach: Proposes TRIDENT combining GCN spatial embeddings with temporal features via Dual-Attention Encoder, using Distance-preserving Multi-kernel Triplet Loss for metric learning.
contribution: Outperforms strong baselines in retrieval accuracy, efficiency, cross-domain generalization, and enables tactical analysis of sports via silhouette-guided clustering.

problem: While AI-generated text detection exists, distinguishing AI-edited text from human-written and fully AI-generated text remains unexplored.
approach: Proposes using lightweight similarity metrics to quantify AI editing magnitude, training EditLens regression model to predict amount of AI editing present.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art with F1=94.7% (binary) and F1=90.4% (ternary) classification, with applications to authorship attribution and education.

problem: Integrating diverse patient data modalities for Alzheimer's diagnosis requires effective interaction among uni-modal foundation models without disrupting pre-trained representations.
approach: Proposes framework enabling joint interaction via modality-anchored interaction, using modality-aware Q-formers to map auxiliary features into anchor model's feature space.
contribution: Consistently outperforms prior methods on AD diagnosis and progression prediction across four modalities (sMRI, fMRI, clinical records, genetic data).

problem: While geographic Implicit Neural Representations embed location data into high-dimensional embeddings, understanding information content concentration remains unclear.
approach: Provides first study of intrinsic dimensionality of geographic INRs, analyzing how ambient dimension relates to actual information-bearing dimensions.
contribution: Shows intrinsic dimensions fall between 2-10 for ambient dimensions 256-512, correlate with task performance, and enable unsupervised model evaluation.

problem: LLMs provide overconfident responses despite insufficient patient information in clinical settings, lacking systematic strategies to identify knowledge boundaries.
approach: Proposes KnowGuard with investigate-before-abstain paradigm, integrating systematic knowledge graph exploration for evidence discovery and evaluation.
contribution: Enables reliable identification of insufficient medical evidence and systematic reasoning path tracing on multi-round clinical benchmarks.

problem: Extracting structured information from semi-structured HTML content at web-scale is challenging, with existing methods lacking generalization or being resource-intensive.
approach: Introduces SCRIBES reinforcement learning framework generating reusable extraction scripts leveraging layout similarity across structurally similar webpages.
contribution: Outperforms baselines by over 13% in script quality and boosts GPT-4o question answering accuracy by over 4% on CommonCrawl data.

problem: Scaling RL to tens of thousands of parallel environments requires exploration, but merely broadening exploration space doesn't enhance learning if excessive exploration reduces quality.
approach: Theoretically analyzes impact of inter-policy diversity on learning efficiency, proposes Coupled Policy Optimization (CPO) regulating diversity through KL constraints.
contribution: Outperforms SAPG, PBT, and PPO across dexterous manipulation tasks in both sample efficiency and final performance with structured exploratory behavior.

problem: Graph neural networks deployed in sensitive applications require ability to remove data upon GDPR request, but lacks principled benchmark for evaluating unlearning methods.
approach: Presents first systematic benchmark for GNN unlearning structured around efficiency, utility, and forgetting across diverse datasets and deletion scenarios.
contribution: Shows most unlearning techniques are impractical for large-scale graphs, provides actionable guidelines for selecting methods and identifies when unlearning is viable.

problem: Traditional Generator-Evaluator ranking approaches scale poorly with combinatorially large candidate spaces, with performance gains saturating quickly.
approach: Proves generator-only models achieve smaller approximation error than multi-generator-evaluator models, proposes GoalRank using reward models as reference policy.
contribution: One-stage framework outperforms multi-generator baselines with better scaling properties, validated through offline experiments and large-scale online A/B tests.

problem: Vision-language models face challenges understanding near-infinite video streams without escalating latency and memory usage due to quadratic computational costs.
approach: Introduces StreamingVLM maintaining compact KV cache by reusing attention sink states, recent vision tokens, and recent text tokens via inference-aligned training.
contribution: Achieves 66.18% win rate against GPT-4O mini on Inf-Streams-Eval benchmark with 2-hour videos, maintaining 8 FPS real-time performance on single H100.

problem: Small language models struggle with complex knowledge-intensive tasks requiring structured reasoning and effective retrieval despite being attractive for cost-sensitive settings.
approach: Proposes FutureMind, modular framework equipping SLMs with thinking-pattern priors via adaptive knowledge distillation, with four-module dynamic reasoning pipeline.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on multi-hop QA benchmarks under zero-training conditions, revealing cognitive bias bottleneck as limiting factor in reasoning transfer.

problem: Detecting AI-generated videos requires both accurate classification and interpretable explanations for transparency, with limited datasets and evaluation approaches.
approach: Introduces VidGuard-R1, fine-tuning MLLM via GRPO with specialized reward models targeting temporal artifacts, trained on 140k real and AI-generated videos.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot performance on benchmarks, exceeding 95% accuracy with training, delivering precise and interpretable detection rationales.

problem: Transformer language models are typically studied as language recognizers, but their actual use as probabilistic language models generating autoregressively remains theoretically uncharacterized.
approach: Characterizes probability distributions expressible by autoregressive transformer language models, showing how autoregressive and probabilistic transformations affect expressivity.
contribution: Teases apart what functions transformers express in their most common use-case, revealing differences from non-probabilistic settings.

problem: Designing efficient architectural backbones for foundation models requires understanding how attention mechanisms relate to memory retention and optimization.
approach: Reconceptualizes neural architectures as associative memory modules with attentional bias, formalizing internal memory objectives and presenting Miras framework.
contribution: Different Miras designs yield models with varying strengths; instances outperform Transformers on language modeling, reasoning, recall, and time series tasks.

problem: Claims of LLM self-awareness and sentience lack rigorous scientific measurement, hindering assessment of safety and policy implications.
approach: Introduces novel methodology quantitatively evaluating metacognitive abilities in LLMs, testing ability to strategically deploy knowledge of internal states.
contribution: Frontier LLMs show increasingly strong metacognitive abilities including confidence assessment and answer anticipation, but abilities are limited in resolution and context-dependent.
